Level 1 · Foundations

Level 1: Software Architecture Foundations

What software architecture is and how to practise it on a small system: requirements, quality, design, description and analysis, with exam readiness built in.

Open the courseSee pathways

Live online course US$149

Who it is for
Developers, aspiring architects and IT professionals who take part in software projects and want to design, describe and assess architecture for small and medium systems.
Before you start
No earlier level. Some experience building or maintaining software helps, and basic UML (the Unified Modeling Language) and object-oriented ideas are assumed.
Capstone evidence
One architecture file for a system you know, built across all 14 lessons, and a mock-exam readiness report.
How it is assessed
Five quiz questions per lesson, a lab health check of six items, and five timed mock exams. The certificate shows you finished the course; it is not proctored.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your record.

ModuleWhat it coversEvidence
Basic conceptsDefinitions, goals, the architect’s role and the people around it.A glossary and a one-page statement of the architect’s role
Requirements, constraints and qualityWhat shapes the design before you draw anything.Stakeholder list, constraints and measurable quality scenarios
Design and developmentApproaches, principles, patterns, interfaces, runtime, deployment and cross-cutting rules.Decomposition, interface and data-model sketches with reasons
Specification and communicationViews, notations, decision records and arc42 as one practical structure.Context, building-block, runtime and deployment views
Analysis and a worked exampleTest a design with evidence, then trace three requirements end to end.A short assessment of the design against its own scenarios
AI and exam readinessVerify what AI tools produce, then practise under exam conditions.A verified AI-use note and a readiness report from the mock exams
